opening.text: Picture a map in a big mall. It has a star that says “You are here.” The map is no help until you know where you are and where you want to go.
Life works the same way. Today I want to talk about why we are here.

mainMessage.text: God sent us here on purpose. We are here to learn, to be tested, to find joy, and to become more like Jesus Christ. Each of us also has good work to do. When we know this, everyday life makes more sense.

blocks.text: You are here for a reason.
Before this life, God said He would prove us to see if we would follow Him. This life is the time to prepare to meet Him.

And we will prove them herewith, to see if they will do all things whatsoever the Lord their God shall command them; And they who keep their first estate shall be added upon; and they who keep not their first estate shall not have glory in the same kingdom with those who keep their first estate; and they who keep their second estate shall have glory added upon their heads for ever and ever.
For behold, this life is the time for men to prepare to meet God; yea, behold the day of this life is the day for men to perform their labors.
President Thomas S. Monson said this in his talk “Finding Joy in the Journey” from the October 2008 general conference.
His glorious gospel provides answers to life’s greatest questions: Where did we come from? Why are we here?
The gospel answers the question, and we can trust the answer.
God wants you to be happy.
Lehi taught that we are here to have joy. Jesus Christ said He came so that we could have life, and have it in full.
Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.
The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.

President Dieter F. Uchtdorf of the First Presidency said this in his talk “Happiness, Your Heritage” at the general Relief Society meeting in September 2008. It was given at that meeting, not in a regular conference session.
Our birthright—and the purpose of our great voyage on this earth—is to seek and experience eternal happiness.
Joy is not a side effect. It is part of the plan.
Joy has a source.
God’s own work is about us. He wants us to live forever with Him. And He promises to finish what He starts in us.
For behold, this is my work and my glory—to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.
The Lord will perfect that which concerneth me: thy mercy, O Lord, endureth for ever: forsake not the works of thine own hands.
President Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Joy and Spiritual Survival” from the October 2016 general conference.

When the focus of our lives is on God’s plan of salvation . . . and Jesus Christ and His gospel, we can feel joy regardless of what is happening—or not happening—in our lives. Joy comes from and because of Him. He is the source of all joy.
Joy comes from Jesus Christ, so it can reach us even on hard days.
Your life can look like His.
We were made to do good. Paul said we were created for good works. Jesus Christ asked us to let our light shine.
For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.
Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
President Ezra Taft Benson said this in his article “Jesus Christ—Gifts and Expectations” in the December 1988 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.

That man is greatest and most blessed and joyful whose life most closely approaches the pattern of the Christ. This has nothing to do with earthly wealth, power, or prestige. The only true test of greatness, blessedness, joyfulness is how close a life can come to being like the Master, Jesus Christ. He is the right way, the full truth, and the abundant life.
Greatness is measured by how close we come to Jesus Christ.
Love is the work.
The first great commandment is to love God. The second is to love others. When we serve people, we serve God.

Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
And behold, I tell you these things that ye may learn wisdom; that ye may learn that when ye are in the service of your fellow beings ye are only in the service of your God.
Elder M. Russell Ballard of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Finding Joy through Loving Service” from the April 2011 general conference.
The love the Savior described is an active love. It is not manifested through large and heroic deeds but rather through simple acts of kindness and service.
Simple kindness is a real purpose.
Small things count.
We do not need a big stage. We need to be anxiously engaged, a little at a time.
Verily I say, men should be anxiously engaged in a good cause, and do many things of their own free will, and bring to pass much righteousness;
Wherefore, be not weary in well-doing, for ye are laying the foundation of a great work. And out of small things proceedeth that which is great.
President Thomas S. Monson said this in his talk “Finding Joy in the Journey” from the October 2008 general conference.
Let us relish life as we live it, find joy in the journey, and share our love with friends and family.
Do a little good today, and enjoy the road.

story.title: Esther, for such a time as this

blocks.text: Esther was a queen, and she was afraid to speak up for her people. Her cousin Mordecai sent her this message.

For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place; but thou and thy father’s house shall be destroyed: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
Esther did not know her purpose until the moment came. Then she spoke, and her people were saved. Our purpose often shows up the same way, in the moment right in front of us.

story.title: Well done, good and faithful servant

blocks.text: In a parable, a master gave his servants money to look after. One servant used it well. The master said this to him.
His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.
The servant was praised for being faithful in a few things. He was not praised for being famous. And the reward was joy. That is the purpose and the prize together.

story.title: About my Father’s business

blocks.text: When Jesus was twelve, His parents found Him in the temple after searching for three days. He said this to them.
And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business?

For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.

The only true test of greatness, blessedness, joyfulness is how close a life can come to being like the Master, Jesus Christ. He is the right way, the full truth, and the abundant life.
He walked it first, so we know it can be done.
Help the one behind you.
Good hikers reach back to help the next person. The two great commandments say the same thing. Love God, and love the people near you.

Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
And behold, I tell you these things that ye may learn wisdom; that ye may learn that when ye are in the service of your fellow beings ye are only in the service of your God.
Elder M. Russell Ballard of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Finding Joy through Loving Service” from the April 2011 general conference.

A hand held out is a simple act with great meaning.

Wherefore, be not weary in well-doing, for ye are laying the foundation of a great work. And out of small things proceedeth that which is great.

story.title: God meant it unto good

blocks.text: Joseph was sold by his brothers and spent years in Egypt. Many years later, he spoke to them with kindness.
But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

story.title: I have finished the work

blocks.text: Near the end of His mortal life, Jesus Christ prayed to His Father.
I have glorified thee on the earth: I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do.
Jesus Christ knew His purpose the whole way. He did what God asked, and He could say it was finished. Our work is smaller, but it is ours. We can finish it one day at a time.

application.text: First, name one thing you think God may be asking you to do. Second, take one step on it this week. Third, thank God at the end of the day for what you finished.

blocks.text: I know that God planned this trip for us. I know He wants us to arrive home with joy. I know that Jesus Christ made the way. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
